summary.one_liner: UFO³ is Microsoft's multi-device agent framework (Galaxy) that decomposes requests into DAGs of tasks run across Windows, Linux and Android devices, built on top of the UFO² Windows desktop agent.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes two components: Galaxy (UFO³), a multi-device orchestration framework where a ConstellationAgent decomposes a user request into a DAG of tasks, assigns them to registered devices by platform and capability, and runs them asynchronously with dependency tracking and dynamic DAG editing. Devices communicate with the orchestrator over a WebSocket-based Unified Agent Interaction Protocol (AIP), and device agents are built from a template with MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool integration. UFO² is the single-device Windows agent, combining Windows UIA/Win32/COM control with GUI and API actions, and it can act as a Windows device agent inside Galaxy. The README also includes a comparison table, migration notes, quick-start commands (pip install, config files, `python -m galaxy --interactive`) and LLM configuration examples for OpenAI and Azure OpenAI. It lists citations to the UFO, UFO² and UFO³ papers.
use_cases: cross-device GUI automation on Windows, Linux and Android
automate Windows desktop applications with an LLM agent
run parallel multi-step workflows as a task DAG
research on GUI agents and multi-agent orchestration
integrate MCP tools into device agents
how_to_run: copy config\galaxy\agent.yaml.template config\galaxy\agent.yaml, then add API keys
Start device agents (server, MCP servers and client) per platform-specific guides
For UFO² standalone: copy config\ufo\agents.yaml.template to config\ufo\agents.yaml, then python -m ufo --task <task>
notable: Galaxy (UFO³) decomposes requests into a DAG of TaskStars with dependencies and supports runtime DAG rewriting
UFO² is marked LTS, and the README says it can serve as a Windows device agent for Galaxy
UFO² reports a 51% reduction in LLM calls via speculative multi-action
Custom device agents are built from a template with MCP integration
caveats: Galaxy is described as active development; some components such as advanced device types and enhanced monitoring are still in development
Galaxy setup is rated moderate difficulty and requires configuring LLM API keys and each device agent
UFO² is documented as Windows-only for its desktop agent
